phase_name: Canonical Human Governance Record Contract Independent Verification
summary: Independently re-derived and adversarially verified CHGR-001 v1.0 (docs/contracts/CANONICAL_HUMAN_GOVERNANCE_RECORD_CONTRACT.md) without trusting Phase 143A or Phase 143B's own conclusions, mirroring the role-separated re-derivation discipline of Phase 142B/142E/142H and 137X/137ZA. Read Phase 143A's Architecture (992 lines) in full before re-reading CHGR-001's own prose; spot-checked the five framework contracts (GLP-001, GAC-001, PGP-001, PPA-001, AGOC-001) at every provision CHGR-001 cites (GLP-001 section 0 and section 8, GAC-REQ-042/043, AGOC-REQ-002); read TAMC-001 and TAMPC-001 directly at every requirement number CHGR-001 section 19.1 cites (TAMC-REQ-005/024/025/036, TAMPC-REQ-002/010/011); read GPC6-REQ-040's own table (docs/contracts/GLP_PILOT_C6_STAGE2_CONTRACT.md section 9) directly rather than trusting CHGR-001's own characterization of it; and re-read docs/GPC6_REQ_075B_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_ELECTION.md in full. Ran all twenty verification passes the governing prompt required: purpose verification, architecture conformance (section-by-section trace against 143A's seventeen invariants/nine workflow stages/twelve template fields/eight-state lifecycle/six assurance levels/ten-item legacy-import discipline/compatibility table/governance table), requirement-set structural verification (full extraction confirming all 193 CHGR-REQ-### identifiers unique, sequential, gap-free; duplicate/near-duplicate scan; hidden-dependency scan; circular-reference scan), human-authorship adversarial probes (AI-pre-filled rationale, AI-selected-option-with-preview, history-based inference), interactive-decision scenario tests (Enter key, timeout, session loss, abandoned session, partial completion, duplicated confirmation), authority-derivation vector tests (nine vectors: filename, location, commit history, digest match, signature presence, formatting, repository presence, publication alone, provenance alone -- all nine independently confirmed explicitly forbidden by a named requirement, not merely implied), provenance/authority distinction check, lifecycle illegal-transition tests (Published to Draft, Revoked to Published, Superseded to Active, Published to Edited -- all four prevented), legacy-import scenario tests cross-checked directly against the actual election record's own text, phase-separation verification, runtime-boundary self-authorization probe, governance-responsibility citation re-derivation (surfaced NB-1), compatibility re-derivation from TAMC-001/TAMPC-001's own frozen text rather than 143A's summary, security scenario table (14 named scenarios), audit-sufficiency check against the actual election record, requirement-coverage analysis, completeness review, and adversarial-governance review (7 attacker profiles). Found two Non-Blocking findings: NB-1, CHGR-001 section 20 cites GPC6-REQ-040 as already defining a generic 'Human Authority' role concept usable across every Human Governance Act class, but GPC6-REQ-040's own table (and its source, GLP-001 section 8) actually define a narrower, GLP-PILOT-C6/GLP-stage-progression-scoped role -- assessed non-operative since CHGR-001 section 6/CHGR-REQ-051 already requires each Decision Template to independently name its own eligible authority regardless of this citation, so no template can actually rely on the imprecise citation in practice; NB-2, a self-referential citation at CHGR-REQ-154 (its own 'see also' parenthetical cites CHGR-REQ-154 itself), a non-normative drafting typo with no correctly-reconstructable intended target. Also disclosed seven Observations (OBS-1 through OBS-7): CHGR-REQ-103/105 assurance-overclaiming redundancy; CHGR-REQ-147's six-item verification-sequence compression relative to 143A section 9.4's seven-item ordered list; CHGR-REQ-034's inference-scope phrasing reading narrower in isolation than section 4's fuller intent; session-loss/browser-refresh not named as explicitly as timeout/Enter-key are; absence of an explicit unlinked-same-subject-conflicting-CHGR detection requirement; absent retention/archival sections traced to an already-disclosed 143A scope boundary, not a CHGR-001-introduced gap; and an undisclosed distributed-repository-clone-staleness gap with currently no attack surface since no runtime consumer exists yet. Neither Non-Blocking finding was repaired in-contract this phase: NB-1 requires a substantive re-citation deserving deliberate review rather than a same-phase drive-by edit, and NB-2's correct intended target cannot be confidently reconstructed without guessing at 143B's original drafting intent -- both disclosed for a future dedicated repair phase or 143D's own planning-stage acknowledgment, consistent with treating CHGR-001 as a hypothesis to invalidate rather than silently patching during the same pass that found the defect. Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. CHGR-001 v1.0's text is byte-identical to its 143B-frozen state; no docs/contracts/**  file was modified; docs/GPC6_REQ_075B_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_ELECTION.md was read only, never modified; no schema, CLI, storage, migration, or signing mechanism was implemented; no runtime enforcement or authority-resolution behavior was implemented or changed; no election or GAC-001 section 9 decision was made, simulated, or presumed. Full fast_green test tier (4391 tests) passed with no regression. Runtime confirmed unchanged (Observed / observe / unavailable) via pcae runtime inspect before and after this phase. See docs/PHASE_143C_CANONICAL_HUMAN_GOVERNANCE_RECORD_CONTRACT_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md.
